One face is thermally insulating. The other has very good thermal contact with the gas: molecules of mass \(m\) acquire the disk temperature in a single collision with that surface.
Estimate the initial acceleration \(a_0\) and maximum speed \(v_{\max}\) during the subsequent motion.

The disk heat capacity is of order \(Nk_B\), where \(N\) is its number of atoms and \(k_B\) is Boltzmann's constant. The molar masses of gas and disk material are of the same order. The gas mean free path is much larger than the disk. Neglect edge effects.

2. Disk in gas
A thin flat disk of mass \(M\), face area \(S\) and temperature \(T_1\) is initially at rest in weightlessness in a gas of mass density \(\rho\) and temperature \(T_0\), with \(T_1=1000T_0\). One face is thermally insulating. The other has very good thermal contact with the gas: molecules of mass \(m\) acquire the disk temperature in a single collision with that surface.
Estimate the initial acceleration \(a_0\) and maximum speed \(v_{\max}\) during the subsequent motion.
The disk heat capacity is of order \(Nk_B\), where \(N\) is its number of atoms and \(k_B\) is Boltzmann's constant. The molar masses of gas and disk material are of the same order. The gas mean free path is much larger than the disk. Neglect edge effects.

solution.text:
2. Disk in gas
Initial acceleration
Let \(n=\rho/m\). The pressure on the insulating face is \(P_0=nk_BT_0\): the incident molecular flux is proportional to the incoming normal speed \(v_{x0}\), and an elastic collision transfers momentum \(2mv_{x0}\). On the hot face the incident flux is initially the same, but the outgoing normal speed is of order \(v_{x1}\sim\sqrt{k_BT_1/m}\). Each collision transfers \(m(v_{x0}+v_{x1})\sim mv_{x1}\). Consequently, up to order-one numerical factors,
\[P_1\sim nk_B\sqrt{T_0T_1}\gg P_0,\quad F\sim Snk_B\sqrt{T_0T_1},\quad a_0\sim\frac{S\rho k_B\sqrt{T_0T_1}}{mM}.\]
The disk accelerates away from the hot face. It is incorrect to use the equilibrium pressure at the hot temperature, since the incident molecular flux is fixed by the cold gas.
Maximum speed
Once the disk moves at a speed comparable to \(v_0=\sqrt{k_BT_0/m}\), the molecular flux catching its hot rear face drops very rapidly because of the Maxwell velocity distribution. The source gives rough flux ratios of \(10^{-3}\) at \(2v_0\) and \(10^{-6}\) at \(3v_0\). This suppresses the initial pressure bias of order \(\sqrt{T_1/T_0}\simeq30\). Thus
\[v_{\max}\sim\sqrt{\frac{k_BT_0}{m}}.\]
Check that cooling is slow
The acceleration time and initial heat-removal power scale as
\[t_a\sim\frac{v_{\max}}{a_0}\sim\frac{M}{\rho S}\sqrt{\frac{m}{k_BT_1}},\qquad P_{\rm th}\sim Snk_BT_1\sqrt{\frac{k_BT_0}{m}}.\]
The initial heat content is \(Q\sim Nk_BT_1\), and the comparable atomic masses give \(M\sim Nm\). Therefore
\[t_c\sim\frac{Q}{P_{\rm th}}\sim\frac{M}{\rho S}\sqrt{\frac{m}{k_BT_0}},\qquad \frac{t_a}{t_c}\sim\sqrt{\frac{T_0}{T_1}}\ll1.\]
The initial heat-loss power is maximal, so Q divided by that power gives a lower estimate for the cooling time. The source calls it an upper bound, but the inequality direction is reversed. The slow-cooling conclusion is preserved. The two automatic fields check the source's scaling estimates with the order-one coefficients set to one. They do not assess the accuracy of a kinetic-theory prefactor or replace the reasoning. The original marking scheme is in the reference PDF.
